title: Family music, a cornet at four, siblings and his father's Navy clarinet
summary: Everyone played by ear in the evenings; his grandfather gave him a cornet at four. He lost a brother in the flu epidemic, and his father was a Navy clarinetist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What kind of instruments would they play?

Well, mostly violin, banjos, mandolins, guitars and when I was four my grandfather Maxwell, my father's father, gave me a cor-net. One of my uncles played cor-net and one played baritone horn. But they played mostly old Scotch-Irish songs or they played country music. My grandfather played country fiddle. He held it down on his stomach and played on his stomach, like a bass viol. And my mother played violin, but she had gone to Conservatory. She was a good violinist. So we all sat around and played in the evening, by ear, everything.
Were there any brothers or sisters? You mentioned it was a large family.

Well, it was but I had a brother who died in 1919 in a flu epidemic. And then I had a sister born in 1920, Marjorie, who is still alive. Then there was no children until 1932, I had another sister, which was born in 1932 and she died last year, 1978. My sister Marjorie is still alive.
But none of them -- Marjorie tinkled around the piano but none of them were very interested in music. My father was a very good clarinetist. He told me he was known as the Boy Wonder in the Navy.
Oh, he was in the Navy?
He ran away from home in the 6th grade and joined the Navy. He was very big for his age. And maybe he was very old for the 6th grade, too. I don't know.
